Hi Rachel —

I've attached a quick p99 heatmap and a short timeline from our end. Can you triage? If this looks like a Redwood-side backpressure issue, we need an ETA and whether we should pause traffic to the feature.

Thanks,

On Fri, 19 Jul 2029 at 08:28, Rachel Kim wrote:
> Thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I’m pulling the ops team in now.

Quick summary from ops after an initial look:

- Observed pattern: prefix growth / queue accumulation on payments-inference (variant: pay-v2-quant) starting ~02:12 UTC, aligned with OrchidPay spike.
- Root cause hypothesis: an internal concurrency cap on the model worker group plus a degraded KV-cache hit rate. A combination produced sustained request queuing that amplified p99.
- Evidence: long tail of enqueued requests (see attached CSV), and a cluster of 5xx-timeouts originating from worker eviction during GC windows.

Short-term recommendations (we can action now):
1) Temporarily lift concurrency cap for pay-v2-quant from 24 -> 36 (adds capacity quickly).
2) Enable request-shed (graceful rejection) on non-critical debug routes to preserve inference capacity for checkout.
3) Route a % of traffic to pay-v2-fp16 fallback variant that has lower latency under concurrency.

We're prepping traces and a more complete timeline. Ben, can you confirm whether increasing the cap will cause downstream pressure on other shared pools?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Claire Horton <claire.horton@orchidpay.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2029 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unusual p99 escalations after last-night's deploy

On Fri, 19 Jul 2029 at 09:03, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Quick summary from ops after an initial look:

Confirming initial findings and adding infra detail:

- The worker pool for pay-v2-quant was auto-scaled conservatively after the model onboarding change; autoscaler window set at 2m and concurrency cap enforced in the serving shim. Under the fast burst from OrchidPay the cap hit and kept requests in the router queue.
- KV-cache churn: increased cold misses by ~28% for the last-token prefixes (we saw increased memcpy/alloc during GC spikes which amplified CPU contention).
- Short-term mitigation tradeoffs: lifting the cap to 36 on pay-v2-quant is safe for the next 3 hours and should collapse the queue; we should simultaneously shift 15% traffic to pay-v2-fp16.
- Longer-term: we should tune autoscaler aggressiveness, add a per-customer routing circuit-breaker, and add a KV pre-warming step for new prefix patterns that OrchidPay introduced.

I will schedule the cap bump now and push a routing change. Expect visible p99 reduction within ~8 minutes; will post traces when available.

—Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: orchidpay_audit_excerpt.txt

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Exec note: OrchidPay p99 spike — short capacity request + credit consideration

Laura —

FYI and asking for quick approval: OrchidPay is experiencing a customer-visible p99/regression tied to queue accumulation on pay-v2-quant after their traffic pattern changed post-deploy. Ops/infra propose a temporary concurrency-cap increase (24 -> 36) + 15% traffic shift to pay-v2-fp16. Expected impact: collapse queue and reduce p99 within ~10 minutes.

Ask: approval to (1) authorize a short-term (4 hour) capacity bump on the dedicated pool serving OrchidPay and (2) approve a one-off account credit if the degradation meets our SLA impact window. This will be time-limited and we will follow up with a root-cause readout and permanent mitigations (autoscaler tuning, circuit-breaker).

If approved I’ll coordinate with Ben and Marissa on the change and communicate timing to OrchidPay.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
